svg.text: One tilting main spindle holds a potato between centres (lathe) or a vessel by its base ring (bowl, drum, pour, wash).
wet cell 800 W × 520 D × 1000 H (module 900 W)
12 axes · S1 20 Nm / 1500 rpm · trunnion B ±95°
peel 20 s per potato (1.5 kg in 3.5 min)
FRONT VIEW of the wet cell (door removed)
workpiece turns, a floating blade with a depth shoe follows the uneven surface; peel falls to the chip chute
feed 8 mm/rev → 80 mm in 3 s · peel ≈ 15 %, end caps ≈ 5 % (faced off by the parting knife)
onion: the same lathe draws 24 radial cuts, then the parting knife slices every 5 mm → dice
One trunnion, one vessel, five jobs
tilting the spindle turns the same pallet into lathe, bowl, drum, pour/flip and washer
1/8 The box dock tilts: potatoes roll down the chute onto the helical brush rollers (wash, singulate, align).
2/8 The rollers lift one potato onto the lathe axis; the tailstock S2 closes and clamps it on the spur.
3/8 Lathe mode: S1 turns the potato, the peel blade on the tool bar travels along it; the flap sends peel to the chip chute.
4/8 The parting knife faces the ends, the flap flips, S2 opens: the peeled potato drops down the part chute into the vessel.
5/8 Bowl mode B +90°: a vessel sits on the faceplate and turns; the roller tool on the quill stands still — kneading.
6/8 Drum mode B +30°, lid on: the vessel tumbles the salad slowly (15 rpm), dressing through the lid port.
7/8 Pour mode B −95°: the vessel tips over the pot on the floor and empties; the same move dump-flips a pan.
8/8 Wash: the bare faceplate spins at 1500 rpm and throws a water sheet; sweeping B ±95° sprays ceiling, walls and floor.
